title: Distance on the invariant set is p-adic, not Euclidean

statements.text: The natural measure of distance on $I_U$ is a $p$-adic metric for a large finite prime $p$. Under it, perturbations that look conspiratorially small in the Euclidean metric take points off $I_U$ and are unphysically large.

sources.quote: certain key perturbations which seem conspiratorially small relative to the more traditional Euclidean metric, take points away from $I_U$ and are therefore unphysically large
